External settlement and financial dynamics across the ready closures

Published

October 1, 2026

Written: 2026-10-01 · Starting repo: main @ 80094f9.

What the comparison establishes

The same expenditure-switching impulse is applied to each ready external closure on the EU/Rest-of-World and North/South workbooks. A stationary baseline does not establish that a disturbed economy returns to that baseline. The external settlement rule determines whether the disturbance accumulates in financial stocks, changes government spending, or moves the exchange rate. This report separates the observed responses from the roots expected from the equations; the subsequent transition-matrix analysis measures those roots directly.

An arm is one runnable row of data/arms.csv. Z1/Z2 mean EU/RoW on the canonical workbook and North/South on the alternative workbook. All displayed numerical tables and the figure are recomputed from the named input CSVs when this report renders.

Monetary hierarchy and the settlement mechanism

reserve_spec identifies which central bank can hold the other region’s bills; membership and monetary hierarchy are separate choices. Under gold settlement its directional label has no active reserve-bill role. Under fiat it identifies the reserve holder; under OPENFIXG that holder’s government adjusts. This implements the mechanisms discussed in Godley–Lavoie chapter 12 as documented in log/trackers/closure_region.md and qmd/equations/closure_overrides.csv.

Closure What absorbs imbalance Equation-based root expectation Variable carrying a scenario’s external effect
OPENFIX-gold Central-bank gold, fixed exchange rate Debt/gold level directions can retain a unit root Gold and cumulative public-debt changes
OPENFIX-fiat Reserve holder’s foreign bills, gold fixed The isolated reserve-interest recursion has multiplier \(1+r_b\) Foreign-bill reserves and their interest circuit
OPENFIXG Reserve holder’s real government spending Feedback is expected to remove the accumulating external mode; other roots remain to be measured Adjusting government’s spending
Quasi-float Exchange rate reacts to lagged current account; gold still settles Depends on par_xr and the trade/financial feedback Exchange rate, with residual gold/debt effects

These are mechanism predictions from model/code/MVP_model_2026.R, not measured eigenvalues. For fiat, \(R_{t+1}=(1+r_b)R_t+f_t\) describes the isolated reserve-interest circuit; an endogenous \(f_t\) can change the coupled system’s root. OPENFIXG’s expected stabilisation must likewise be checked on the full system rather than inferred from a stationary cache.

Measured baselines

The fiat file supersedes earlier fiat rows. Debt/VA is outstanding government bills divided by nominal value added in the same region’s currency. CAB/VA is the current-account flow divided by that same value added. The slope is OLS of debt/VA on period over the final baseline window, as defined in R/closures/closure_baseline_stability.R. Gold is quantity; foreign reserves are bills in the issuer’s currency. NA means the mirror reserve row does not exist, not zero holdings.

The one-period export impulse

R/closures/impulse_closure.R switches 10% of each Z2 household consumption share in its own-origin good to the corresponding Z1-origin good in period 70 only. Each industry’s total share is preserved; this is a change of origin, not a rise in household expenditure. Period 71 restores the original exogenous shares. The impulse CSV covers periods 68 through 100, and the pre-shock rows have zero differences for every arm. The figure includes both regions of every ready cell; exchange rate is Z1_xr in both region records, intentionally duplicated by the measurement script.

Interpretation. Under gold, a persistent stock displacement after the flow impulse subsides is consistent with a neutral level mode. Under fiat, the reserve displacement exposes the interest-bearing settlement channel. Under OPENFIXG, the spending adjustment is the external transmission channel. The quasi-float shows the exchange-rate response at the registry’s existing par_xr; its horizon does not establish global stability or choose that parameter. A finite impulse is not an infinitesimal eigenvector experiment, so its final-period response alone cannot identify a root.

OPENFLEX is an unstable control, not a ready impulse cell

The scan contains no stable band. Its growth is a log slope; the multiplicative growth factor is its exponential, not one plus the slope. With portfolio sensitivity switched off, the repeated expectation-adaptation settings produce the same runaway, so expectations alone cannot explain it. The full-adaptation, full-sensitivity run ends early and must not be interpreted using uncomputed final columns. An impulse on such a drifting baseline would mix the impulse with the runaway.

Limits and decisions left open

The unit-root and reserve-interest accounts above are equation-based expectations pending a consistent-manifold stability analysis. All stock differences depend on the baseline calibration and the stated finite horizon. The maintainer retains the decisions on par_xr, the South’s short fiat reserve, scenario 6, and recalibrating the canonical enterprise premium with Ξ. This report makes none of those choices.

Sources: the four CSVs named above; data/arms.csv; R/closures/impulse_closure.R; R/closures/closure_baseline_stability.R; model/code/MVP_model_2026.R; log/trackers/closure_region.md; ai_context/04_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md (closure decisions).
